Route 6 is crucial for Hong Kong’s road network, linking West Kowloon to Tseung Kwan O (TKO) New Town with interchanges at Kai Tak and Lam Tin. The visit will provide an opportunity to learn about the project and its construction. Upon completion of the entire Route 6, peak-hour journey time between Tseung Kwan O Town Centre and Yau Ma Tei is expected to fall from about 65 minutes to approximately 12 minutes. events.org: Mechanical, Marine, Naval Architecture & Chemical Division
events.venue: Chan Yat Mei Sophie Room, 9/F Island Beverley
events.description: Introduction Firestop systems are passive fire protection measures used to maintain the fire resistance rating of walls, floors, and other fire compartment barriers when penetrated by Mechanical & Electrical (M&E) services such as cables, cable trays, conduits, pipes, ducts, and busbars. During a fire, openings created for building services can allow the spread of flame, smoke, and hot gases between fire compartments. Firestop systems are specifically designed and tested to seal these penetrations and restore the fire performance of the compartment wall or floor. Agenda -> Fire Safety Concept & Design Standard -> Firestop Test -> Proper Installation & Quality check Speaker: Ms. Wong Lai Yan Lillian, Technical Engineering Manager of Engineering Department from Hilti Hong Kong Limited Lillian is the Technical Engineering Manager of Hilti Hong Kong Limited, brings over 14 years of experience in the construction sector. She holds a BEng (Hons) in Product Analysis and Engineering Design from The Hong Kong Polytechnic University and has spent the last 9 years driving complex project engineering, code compliance, and technical approvals at Hilti (HK) Limited.

events.description: Programme Highlights: This seminar introduces the hybrid cooling tower at Black Point Power Station's new Unit D2 combined-cycle gas turbine. It explains why cooling tower was selected over the conventional once-through seawater cooling system, and how the hybrid wet–dry design can minimise plumes. The seminar explains how the cooling tower will lessen environmental impacts by reducing heat rejection to the sea, cutting down seawater intake by about 95%, and avoiding major civil works such as dredging and tunnelling. It also covers how plume, drift, noise and corrosion are managed, the trade-offs in output and efficiency, and the regulatory approach. Participants will gain insights into sustainable cooling design for modern power stations. events.description: Technical Seminar: AI × 5D BIM: The Next Leap in Hong Kong Quantity Surveying's Digital Transformation Date/Time: 18 December 2026 (Friday), 18:30-20:00 Venue: Chan Yat Mei Sophie Room, 9th Floor, Island Beverley, No 1 Great George Street, Causeway Bay Organised by: HKIE Civil Division Automated 5D BIM Quantity Take-off (QTO) has long been a key priority for digitalizing quantity surveying in Hong Kong. Yet conventional BIM-based modelling and quantity calculation face two core obstacles: highly complex local drawings—especially reinforcement detailing—that make manual interpretation and modelling extremely time-consuming, and a critical lack of integration between BIM models and QS measurement rules. With the explosive advancement of artificial intelligence technology, AI-empowered 5D BIM effectively addresses these industry pain points. It intelligently extracts key information from drawings, interprets design logic and automatically generates compliant BIM models, substantially reducing manual workload and labour costs. This presentation showcases the current capabilities of AI in the construction industry, demonstrates how to automate the integration of measurement rules such as SMM4/5 and BS8666 to deliver 5D BIM quantity surveying, and validates the application reliability of AI-driven intelligent quantity take-off with real-world performance results. Overseas Delegation 2027 to Germany – Beyond Carbon: Connecting Green Technologies, Empowering Sustainable Tomorrow
events.venue: Germany
events.description: Overseas Delegation 202 7 to Germany – Beyond Carbon: Connecting Green Technologies, Empowering Sustainable Tomorrow Date, Time & Venue 26 Mar 2027 ( Friday ) – 3 Apr 2027 ( Saturday ) ; Germany Programme Highlights The HKIE-YMC Overseas Delegation is a leadership development programme designed to arouse young engineers’ potential and motivate their vision to learn from overseas experiences and international practices. For the 2026–2027 session, YMC is set to organise an overseas delegation to Germany under the theme ‘ Beyond Carbon: Connecting Green Technologies, Empowering Sustainable Tomorrow ’ focusing on the vital role of engineers in driving decarbonisation through innovative technologies and sustainable frameworks. Germany serves as a compelling international benchmark, highlighted by its national Energiewende policy targeting a climate-neutral economy by 2045 and a minimum 80% share of renewables in gross electricity consumption by 2030. The country actively advances sustainable engineering through its statutory Energy Efficiency Law, heat pump integration, green hydrogen initiatives, passive house engineering, circular economy frameworks, and resilient district planning. Through a blend of technical visits, urban infrastructure studies, and institutional exchanges, the delegation will examine Germany’s holistic approach to low-carbon construction, energy transition, and smart urban infrastructure. Overall, this delegation will provide actionable insights and valuable perspectives that can be adapted to support Hong Kong’s evolving urban transition goals, while fostering bilateral professional links between Hong Kong and German engineering bodies. Delegation Fee HK$ 1 1 ,800 (Air tickets, insurance, accommodation (shared room), meals and local transportation inclusive) Registration & Enquiries Application is open to all HKIE Young Members and the number of delegates is limited to 16. All candidates joining the delegation will go through a screening interview
